reviews.head: 7bc8336ea20af407359358ae3c90bba1954ca665
reviews.object: Destination audit of the positive-length / bounded-edge-count return quantile for TARGET-C-PR950-TRAIN-RETURN-LENGTH-QUANTILE.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: Unbounded canonical C-II quadratic-core sequence; D→∞, R4/D²→r>0; fixed epsilon∈(0,r), theta∈(0,1); all labels including contact isolates retained in population count; actual positive-contact core supplies train paths, actual loaded set B supplies targets; exact canonical bank, depletion, loaded-adjacency and Audit 235 hypotheses apply.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: From the train-bank lower bound, select at least (a_*−o(1))D distinct strict-rhombus trains, each degree ≥ L_D=ell D+O(1). If H_L trains have a terminal unit edge on an actual loaded-hull side, incidence gives L_D|A∩H_L|≤2R_H=O(D^(5/3)), so only O(D^(2/3)) trains are lost. Each remaining train contributes a rail endpoint outside B: if both terminal endpoints were loaded, the loaded-near-unit adjacency premise would make that unit edge an actual loaded hull side, contradicting removal. For the resulting source set X, Audit 235 gives (a_D−5k_D)_+(L_D+1)≤beta k_D²+10k_D for the endpoint-inclusive X-to-B separator. Along a subsequence with x=liminf k_D/D<a_*/5, division by D² yields ell(a_*−5x)≤beta x², hence x≥kappa, the positive root; for x≥a_*/5 the same lower bound is automatic. Deduplicate shared rail vertices for X; the cut inequality counts at most five train rails per core vertex and Menger then gives distinct path starts and B endpoints. Full-source Oler plus isodiametry/perimeter gives n_D≤pi D²/(2sqrt(3))+O(D), including isolates. Vertex-disjoint paths imply sum(s_i+1)≤n_D, so at most pi D/(2sqrt(3)t)+O(1) exceed tD edges. With t=pi/[2sqrt(3)(1−theta)kappa], at least (theta*kappa−o(1))D paths have at most tD contact edges.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: Tried to break the quantile by (a) counting only distinct selected root labels, which can be fewer than trains, (b) allowing shared train roots to invalidate Menger, or (c) excluding isolates from the Oler population. The supplied separator argument counts train rails with multiplicity bounded by five at a cut vertex; Menger uses the deduplicated X, and the full-source Oler bound correctly charges every label. The quantile is aggregate: it does not bound every route or provide an endpoint overlap.
reviews.canonical_dependencies_and_interfaces: C-QUADRATIC-CORE-TRAIN-BANK; C-QUADRATIC-CORE-DISJOINT-TRAIN-RETURNS; C-ALL-BRANCH-HULL-TRAIN-DEPLETION (Audit 206); C-LOADED-NEAR-UNIT-ADJACENCY; C-LONG-TRAIN-SEPARATOR-INEQUALITY (Audit 235); finite full-source Oler. The reviewer reconstructs their composition, not the historical proofs of these inputs.
reviews.inherited_claims_and_unchecked_obligatio: Canonical train-bank asymptotics, Audit 206 depletion bound, loaded adjacency theorem, Audit 235 cut inequality, finite Oler/isodiametric framework were inherited premises. No common-grid attachment, route payment, endpoint overlap, movement, or C-II/Level-I closure was established; both artifacts remain unreviewed/noncanonical.

reviews.head: b321833ec6a10a1a47fee5c717c6b2d2e4752f7d
reviews.object: Unloaded-rigidity-brace inequality for a connected actual-contact subset of the C-II core.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: Canonical selected global source with D≥9; nonisolated positive-contact core V, actual contact graph C, strong active actual-diameter rows H; X⊂V nonempty and contact-connected, with no endpoint of H in X. All labels are retained in the original source, but this lemma moves only core coordinates.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: The straight unit-contact graph is planar: if two unit edges cross internally with split lengths s,1−s and t,1−t, choose opposite acute sectors with angle φ≤π/2. The sum of the two selected cross-pair squared distances is s²+(1−s)²+t²+(1−t)²−2cosφ[st+(1−s)(1−t)]<2, contradicting unit separation. Triangle-free means each 2-connected block has faces of size ≥4. Euler and 2e≥p+4(f−1) give e_B≤2|V_B|−p_B/2−2; a bridge contributes 2|V_B|−e_B−2=1. The block-cut identity yields 2q−e_X≥2+Σ(p_B/2)+#bridges. Along the block-cut path of a Euclidean diametral pair in X, each 2-connected block’s outer cycle has perimeter ≥2 times the pair distance within that block; each bridge contributes its unit length. Triangle inequality gives 2q−e_X≥diam(P(X))+2. The rigidity matrix on X has rank≤e_X, so its flex kernel dimension is at least 2q−e_X. If the contact cut had fewer than diam(P(X))+2 rows, a nonzero flex survives all cut rows. Extend it by zero to V; no H row touches X. C-ZRF says the mixed C∪H framework has only rigid infinitesimal motions, but the extension vanishes on both endpoints of an active H edge outside X, forcing a rigid motion to be zero. Contradiction; therefore |δ_C(X)|≥diam(P(X))+2.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: Checked X a single vertex (dimension lower bound exactly 2), a bridge path of b edges (2q−e=b+2 and Euclidean diameter≤b), and articulation branches (off-path block terms are nonnegative). Also checked why the anchor condition must be the exact strong-row set H: weak or omitted rows cannot be used to pin the flex. Isolates are outside V and no full-source motion follows.
reviews.canonical_dependencies_and_interfaces: C-ZRF mixed rigidity rank/kernel; C-WOODALL / C-ZRF active diameter count ensuring H nonempty; planar unit-contact geometry derived in this report. The source report’s other train-return quantile, common-grid extraction, Oler estimates, and endpoint linkage are not audited here.
reviews.inherited_claims_and_unchecked_obligatio: No numerical verifier is needed for the block-counting proof. The broader candidate report’s train families, Oler transfer, endpoint assembly, isolate effects, KKT mass, and finite source competitor remain unchecked. This is a brace inequality only, with no positive boundary-contact stress bound and no endpoint.

reviews.head: c0043e3fb9c75b405e75fa462d5c9f2d1a7f1e85
reviews.object: Near-diameter endpoint transverse-spread and midpoint-longitudinal localization, the exact estimates used at deficits s=0 and s=2 downstream.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: Noncollinear global minimum-diameter unit-separated full source; D≥216; full-source hull K with circumcenter o, incenter o′, support h, perimeter P, area A, η=3^(1/4)√D; arbitrary source pair p,x with d≥D−s, s≥0. The report relies on canonical C-FS-GEOM inequalities and full-source circumradius/inradius bounds.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: C-FS-GEOM gives D/2≤R<D/2+η, R−r<η, P≤πD, A>πD²/4−(√3/4)P; |o′−o|<η implies D/2−2η<h<D/2+η. Put g=h−D/2: ∫g=P−πD≤0, |g|<2η. The support-area identity yields E=∫h′²=∫h²−2A<D(P−πD)+8πη²+(√3/2)P≤(17π√3/2)D. Since h≤D for D≥216 and h″+h≥0, h″≥−D; a positive derivative u must persist at least linearly over u/D radians, so u³/(3D)≤E and |h′|<6D^(2/3) (negative derivatives use the backward ramp). For a pair deficit ≤s, endpoint support deficits δ_p,δ_x satisfy δ_p+δ_x=w−d≤s. Tilt the support normal by ε=D^(−1/3); h≤D and sin ε≥ε/2 yield |(p−o)·Jν|, |(x−o)·Jν|≤13D^(2/3)+2sD^(1/3). The midpoint identity gives |(m−o)·ν|≤(3η+s)/2≤2η+s/2. Both signs of the tilt are needed for absolute tangent bounds. No division by s occurs; the formulas therefore include s=0 and s=2.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: Tested the boundary cases: at s=0, d=D forces both support deficits zero and bounds reduce to 13D^(2/3) tangent and ≤3η/2 normal; at s=2 the displayed constants remain finite. A one-sided tilt would not bound absolute tangent coordinate, so the opposite tilt is essential. Tried to infer a count of near-diameter pairs from localization; no multiplicity estimate is present, so that inference fails.

The audit does not re-prove these canonical premises or the separate positive-leaf anchor argument. reviews.head: 58229f8218d1a0c48c7b1981b9e6cde47cfb0bd8
reviews.object: Inclusive floor closure (IFC), contact-loss detection (CLR), and locked contact release (LCR) for a supplied translating-group family.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: Every source label belongs to a fixed or disjoint moving group, all move parallel to v, no old contact joins distinct moving groups, all pair upper/lower constraints are compiled. Contact release floor F_i=max(0,max τ) with allowed height 0 or ≥F_i (strictly >0 when F_i=0). Weak policy A uses weak upper bounds; policy B makes every previously inactive core-core upper constraint strict. LCR additionally assumes canonical C-ZRF core PSD stress/affine kernel, positive diameter loading h≥ceil D≥9, strict inactive core-core caps, and full-source isolate normalization. Generic bound caps must be nonnegative U_i≥0.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: For an intergroup pair with axial/transverse coordinates (a,z), new squared length is z²+(a+s_i−s_j)². Upper safety is exactly two difference inequalities with costs √(D²−z²)−a and √(D²−z²)+a, nonnegative because old length≤D and strictly positive for inactive pairs. A noncontact with |z|≤1 gives one strict lower difference arc of cost |a|−√(1−z²)>0; |z|>1 is automatically separated. A cut contact’s slack is s_i(s_i−τ), so it opens for s_i>τ. Encode each edge by lexicographic cost (c,−k), k=1 marking strictness. A shortest path to zero set has cost (a_i,−m_i), hence every feasible height obeys s_i≤a_i, strictly if m_i>0. Eliminate i if a_i<F_i; if a_i=F_i>0 with m_i>0; or if a_i=F_i=0. The fixed-point complement I is an upper bound on every feasible active support. Conversely choose small ε and heights s_i=a_i−m_iε for I: shortest-path slack w_e=c_e−a_i+a_j≥0 and the lex shortest-path strict-count inequality preserve zero-slack arcs; ε below the minimum positive slack preserves the rest and positive floors. Thus I itself is feasible and is the unique inclusion-largest support. CLR checks any feasible contact loss forces a corresponding group to survive: strict-above-floor loss is obvious; equality at a positive floor can only open a cut contact with τ<F_i; at F_i=0 any positive active height opens τ≤0. Under policy B, if a core group survives but no contact opens, all old contacts are exactly preserved and lower strict arcs preclude new contacts. Its nonconstant 0/1 indicator has positive Ω-energy: zero energy would put it in affine kernel and confine core to two parallel lines with ≤4 hull vertices, contradicting ≥9 loaded diameter endpoints. Nonnegative cross terms plus any selected positive diagonal term imply positive weighted old-diameter deficit; strict inactive core-core caps and isolate normalization prevent a new maximum from replacing the shortened pair. Endpoint either has D′<D or D′=D with fewer actual diameter pairs, contradicting lexicographic minimality.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: The generic IFC statement omits U_i≥0; with one variable F=0 and cap U=−1, its claimed zero endpoint violates the bound while feasible set is empty. That is a genuine abstract wording defect, and I do not accept the theorem for negative caps. In the geometric application U_i=2D>0, so this counterexample does not affect the supplied-source conclusions. Checked the strict/equal positive-floor distinction: a weak equality path must retain a positive-floor variable; a strict edge at equal cost forces it to zero. Also checked strict inactive caps are load-bearing: if an inactive core pair reaches D, the secondary diameter-pair contradiction is not valid.
reviews.canonical_dependencies_and_interfaces: C-ZRF; C-WOODALL; C-LOADED-HULL; C-FINITE-CONTACT-ISOMETRY-DIAMETER-GAIN for core stress identity (not its stronger noncongruent claim); C-FULL-SOURCE-ISOLATE-NORMALIZATION. All are inherited canonical premises. Finite verifier/control results are recorded by originating audit; no broad rerun here.
reviews.inherited_claims_and_unchecked_obligatio: No owner-family extraction, all-source survivor, asymptotic onset, or universal statement for every canonical minimizer. The generic theorem needs U_i≥0 made explicit; geometric U_i=2D meets it. No promotion.

reviews.head: 277d2d021e8268d90869a09945ac69b04bc18cc2
reviews.object: Finite graph dichotomy between balanced contact/diameter incidence weights and a half-integral separator, plus source-specific strict factor perturbation.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: Finite labeled planar unit-separated source, n≥2, min distance 1, diameter D>1; C and H are disjoint nonempty actual unit-contact and diameter families; every pair outside C∪H has strict 1<d_ij<D. Perturbation concerns the complete abstract pair array.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: Construct states (i,+),(i,−). A contact ij gives arcs i+→j− and j+→i− (and their sign-swapped counterparts); a diameter gives reverse-color arcs i−→j+ and j−→i+. Every arc switches sign, so any directed cycle alternates colors and has even length. Count repeated projected edge occurrences and normalize each color total to one; entering/leaving opposite colors at every visit gives equal incidence at each vertex. For any positive vertex factors s_i, log q′_ij=log q_ij+log s_i+log s_j, and incidence balance cancels all log s terms; the weighted H−C log gap stays log D² and is at most log(max q′/min q′), so no factorized complete-array improvement is possible. If the digraph is acyclic, let w(state) be longest path length to a sink; each arc has w(source)−w(target)≥1. Set z_i=(w(i,+)−w(i,−))/2. Adding paired contact arcs yields z_i+z_j≥1; adding paired diameter arcs yields z_i+z_j≤−1. For every inactive pair, σ=z_i+z_j; if σ<0 choose λ<log d/(-σ), if σ>0 choose λ<log(D/d)/σ. The finite minimum of these positive caps gives one λ>0 preserving all inactive lower/upper constraints while growing contacts and shrinking diameter pairs. This is source-specific formal complete-array endpoint, not a uniform λ.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: The graph helper rejects C/H overlap; D=1 is an excluded boundary where contact and diameter overlap and a pair gives a 2-cycle. A non-unit-separated input with one pair d=1/2 has no contact, so the normalized packing hypothesis is necessary. The six-point pentagon-plus-center control achieves all pair bounds after factorization but centered Gram rank rises 2→3, blocking planar realization. Thus the abstract endpoint cannot be promoted to a geometric competitor.
reviews.canonical_dependencies_and_interfaces: Finite-source normalization and strict inactive margins only; no canonical claim dependency. External planarity/conformal literature is not used in the audited log/convexity proof.
reviews.inherited_claims_and_unchecked_obligatio: No complete E99 historical proof chain, planar realization, global-minimizer statement, or source extraction. The bounded checker census is reported by the submission and not rerun in this intake. The exact next step is a full-source planar competitor or another endpoint lemma.

reviews.head: 3eb24c410dc7a207992aab80fff26a2ddba13d28
reviews.object: Conditional anchor upper box, normal-window deletion, full-source proximity and Type-II owner-count implication.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: C-II canonical source D≥9; supplied disjoint proper core owners with parent translations d_i=δ_i v_i preserving contacts in every binary selection; parent singleton upper safety; each upper-relevant source label including assigned isolates within R of an owner-local crossing loaded diameter anchor; R+ρ≤D/10; cloud/angle constraints ensure Φ<π/2; fixed isolate/exception dispatch; positive-contact-cut owners; for native box w≤π/3. Type-II count additionally assumes supplied stable O–O family, lower-witness localization, every unary and singleton checks, and subfamily stability.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: The phase lemma: two rays from z with lengths ≥D−ε and mutual distance≤D have cosθ≥1−D²/[2(D−ε)²]>0. Center an interval of half-width a=θ/2. Endpoint support defects in a constant-width completion are ≤ε; sublinearity bounds the defect y(t)≤2ε throughout. For support function h of constant-width D, μ=h+h″ satisfies 0≤μ≤D and p=h−D/2 is antiperiodic. Fourier energy E(g)=∫(g′²−g²) is PSD modulo first harmonics; E(p)=2Δ where Δ=πD²/4−area(W); Cauchy–Schwarz gives |∫fg|²≤2ΔE(g), f=p+p″. Test g=cos(t)/cos(a)−1 on the interval, anti-extend by π; with k=tan a−a, E(g)=4k and ∫_I μg≤2εtan a, giving either θ<sqrt(96ε/D) or θ³≤192Δ/D². Canonical area deficit then yields Θ=max(sqrt(96ε/D),(48π√3/D)^(1/3)). For upper safety, contact preservation at binary choices rules out cross-owner contacts; summing KKT over an owner contact cut forces a crossing actual diameter and singleton safety implies its normal has negative projection along owner direction. Delete owners whose anchor normals lie in two perpendicular windows of half-width Φ=w/2+Θ+asin(R/(D−ρ))+asin(ρ/[2(D−ρ)]). Every other owner’s relevant pair vector r to any fixed q has r·v<−ρ/2, so |r+ρv|²<|r|²≤D². Convexity in independent heights extends all corner tests to the box. Partner-independent midpoint localization bounds window occupancy by F_D(Φ)=1+(D sinΦ+2·7D^(2/3))/cosΦ; charge at most two owners per witness edge and 2d_H fixed/exceptions, obtaining ≤2d_H+4 floor F_D(Φ) deletions. If R,ρ=o(D),w=o(1), this is o(D). In no-container branch, F=conv(V) contains inner disk radius (1/2−η)D and source points lie in outer disk radius (1/2+η)D; a near-D partner forces p outside inner radius by at most ρ. Project to boundary and then a loaded side endpoint to get distance ≤D(2η+√(2η))+ρ, only global proximity. The Type-II corollary subtracts AS-deleted owners, invokes Audit106 k≤147(x_B+m_B), then r≤2 floor F_D(Φ)+147(x_B+m_B); it gives o(D) only if the low-defect condition holds.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: The report’s far-label fixture is a direct falsifier of the tempting weaker premise “one good anchor suffices”: a parent singleton is safe but a larger common release violates a formerly inactive upper pair at squared length D²+δ²/2. The exact proof therefore requires same-owner anchor coverage of every upper-relevant label and the fixed isolate dispatch. Also the global proximity lemma supplies a nearby loaded vertex, not an owner-local anchor; the proof itself does not bridge that gap.
reviews.canonical_dependencies_and_interfaces: C-FS-GEOM; C-FS-DIAMETER-MIDPOINT-D2-3; C-LOADED-HULL; C-CII-ACTUAL-DIAMETER-NORMAL-ATOMLESS is cited but the counting uses the stronger partner-independent midpoint estimate; C-WOODALL; C-FULLCORE-NEAR-DISK for proximity branch; Audit106/C-OO-LOWER-WITNESS-OWNER-CAPACITY and its lower-blocker, endpoint-degree, hull-side, isolate-collar prerequisites for Type-II bound. External constant-width characterization is cited for maximal diameter completion; its proof is not imported here.
reviews.inherited_claims_and_unchecked_obligatio: No canonical extraction of supplied owners, owner-local anchor coverage, subfamily-stable O–O family, low-defect condition, strict lower closure, or finite competitor. Verifier fixtures check 744 pair states and far-label regression but not continuum phase lemma/window count/family extraction; their output is in the assigned report, not rerun here.

reviews.head: c020c941f1d86cd174164950134ac1f3c9d05a96
reviews.object: Formal factor-balance obstruction and convex-hull separation equivalence for positive vertex-factor arrays.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: Finite planar unit-separated source with n≥2, D≥1; all pairs q_ij=|p_i−p_j|², actual C and H; nonnegative weights a_e,b_f each total one with equal incidence at every label; arbitrary positive vertex factors s_i; complete pair set used for min/max. For convex-hull converse, D>1 and strict inactive pair gaps are needed.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: For q′_ij=q_ij s_i s_j, weighted log difference is Σ_H b log q′−Σ_C a log q′=log D²: q values contribute log D², and each log s_i cancels by balanced incidence. Since the weighted H average≤log M and C average≥log m over the complete pair extrema, log(M/m)≥log D². For equivalence, convex hulls K_C=conv{e_i+e_j:ij∈C} and K_H=conv{e_i+e_j:ij∈H} intersect exactly when probability weights give coordinatewise equal incidences. If disjoint, strict hyperplane separation supplies x with min_C(x_i+x_j)>max_H(x_i+x_j). Set s_i=e^{t x_i}; at t=0 the extrema lie exactly on C/H, while all other finitely many pairs have strict gaps from 1 and D². For small t>0 extrema stay in C/H and log ratio has negative derivative max_H−min_C, yielding a formal improving complete array. For realized lengths ℓ′_ij=r_i r_j ℓ_ij this applies with s_i=r_i², so the length ratio cannot fall below D.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: Checked that an isolate with zero incidence in both supported families cancels harmlessly and remains in complete extrema; if it is a positive-weight diameter endpoint with no contact incidence, the stated balance premise fails. At D=1 contact and diameter overlap, so the disjoint-color convex-hull/strict-gap converse is outside scope. The exact pentagon-plus-center transformed array has all 15 bounds but centered Gram rank 3, so the formal improving factor array need not be planar. This blocks the geometric overreach.

reviews.head: 48eb6a6caabbf97d4bc681d4a8c2bdd674bfd802
reviews.object: Conditional component anchoring (CA), strict stress gain (SG), and mixed refinement (RM) for supplied owner/translation family.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: Canonical contact-minimal then actual-diameter-pair-minimal C-II source; positive core equilibrium and PSD Ω with affine kernel; disjoint proper owners, exact contact-preserving translations in all binary states, pairwise acute directions; report-specific fixed isolate/anchor/exception dispatch, bounded-face transport, small-cloud bound s<min(D−√(D²−1),√2−1), singleton weak shortening of every actual diameter, all unary strict-rhombus tests, and a nonzero refined state satisfying remaining outer-face lower clauses.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: CA: for a contact component W of a proper owner cut, exact unit-contact preservation gives each crossing contact vector r·d=−|d|²/2. Summing core KKT equilibrium over W cancels internal rows; dot with d gives the crossing positive-diameter resultant dot d=−|d|²/2 times positive contact cut mass<0, hence a positive-multiplier diameter port. Moving a complementary component by −d gives the analogous result. Four binary states on a contact joining two parents have mixed second difference −2d_i·d_j≠0, so no such contact exists. SG: Ω=L_C(α)−L_H+(β) is PSD, ΩP=0, ker Ω=span{1,P_x,P_y}; for disjoint owners, cross indicator energy b_ij equals the sum of positive β on H+ edges crossing them, since contact cross terms vanish, hence b_ij≥0. For κ_i=1_GiᵀΩ1_Gi, PSD gives κ_i≥0; κ_i=0 would put nonconstant 0/1 indicator in affine kernel, placing core on two parallel lines with at most four hull vertices. C-ZRF/Woodall yield ≥ceil D≥9 distinct loaded diameter endpoints, contradiction, so κ_i>0. For nonzero binary selection U=Σx_i1_Gi d_i and exact contacts, Σ_H+β(D²−|Q_h|²)=tr(UᵀΩU)=Σx_iκ_i|d_i|²+2Σx_ix_jb_ij(d_i·d_j)>0. This ensures some supported old diameter shortens only when all rows are already upper-safe; the identity alone is not an upper-feasibility proof. RM: split parent owners into components of C∪H_all; this preserves internal contact and actual-diameter pairs. Cross-owner actual diameters have simultaneous squared change g_i+g_j−2d_i·d_j<0 from singleton g_i,g_j≤0 and acute dot. For inactive pairs, fixed dispatch equalizes displacements on long protected pairs, exception E endpoints are fixed after deleting ≤2d_H owners, and every other pair starts ≤L=√(D²−1) and changes by at most cloud s, so final length≤L+s<D. Lower constraints are covered by parent singleton/strict-rhombus tests, rigid bounded-face transport, and near-unit cofaciality leaving only outer-face clauses. If a nonzero model passes those clauses strictly, no new contact appears; SG gives strict old-diameter loss and upper ledger blocks new diameter, yielding D′<D or fewer actual diameter pairs.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: The finite SR gadget is not a counterexample to canonical RM: its moving component has nonzero contact-cut resultant but no incident diameter row, so it cannot admit the strictly positive KKT equilibrium required by CA/SG; it is explicitly nonglobal and has a smaller square-lattice packing. The eleven zero-limit noncontacts falsify A-only, B-only, and both-owner selections at their critical pairs; hence a nonzero Horn assignment must pass explicit lower clauses, not just implications/unaries. All-large finite H=30,31,100 checks do not by themselves establish the uniform small-t onset; that is supplied by the report’s separate leading-sign argument.

reviews.object: Audit of AB amplitude upper box, CT common translation, UCC implication closure, and IM stress-imbalance estimate for supplied O–O owners.
reviews.hypotheses_and_quantifier_scope: Canonical D≥9 source used only through stated ZRF/Woodall/midpoint/dispatch/localization inputs; supplied disjoint proper core owners, owner translations preserving contacts, acute direction interval, small cloud and angle constraints, every singleton actual-diameter test, fixed isolate/exception dispatch, E bound, positive contact stress and nonnegative diameter stress for IM. UCC compiles every source pair and requires supplied common b that opens every owner-to-fixed contact.
reviews.substantive_reconstruction: AB: unsafe amplification by M of parent singleton yields −Mδ_i/2<r·v_i≤−δ_i/2 for an actual-D witness (with r=moving−fixed). Hence its normal lies in a perpendicular window of half-width asin(Ms/(2D)), plus direction spread w/2. Partner-independent midpoint bounds count ≤F_D(θ_M) loaded endpoints per each of two windows; each endpoint can charge at most two owners, giving 4 floor F_D deletion bound. For surviving owners all binary {0,M} actual-diameter corners are safe: cross-owner joint change is g_i+g_j−2M²d_i·d_j<0; convexity in owner amplitudes fills the box. Inactive full-source pairs are safe by fixed dispatch or length≤L moved by cloud Ms<γ. Contacts have slack x(x−1)δ² under orientation r=moving−fixed; allowed 0 or x≥1 does not shorten them, and x>1 opens some cut contact. This does not cover all-binary selections. CT: exact old contact yields r·v_i=−δ_i/2; with |v−v_i|≤2sin(w/4), translating by common b=ρv gives positive slack ≥ρ(ρ−δ_i−4sin(w/4)). Upper-unsafe witnesses lie in two narrow perpendicular windows; after deletion, all relevant moved/fixed pairs satisfy r·v<−ρ/2, so |r+ρv|²<|r|². Cloud ρ<γ protects inactive pairs; no D pair can cross two retained moving owners because the two singleton changes sum to 2ρ²>0. UCC: for noncontact between owners, singleton lower slacks are c±2r·b+ρ² and sum 2c+2ρ²>0, so at most one lower failure. Each failed singleton state becomes a directed implication; a fixed-label failure is a unary zero; all pairs, including inactive upper pairs, are compiled. Backward reachability from unary blockers is exactly the forced-zero set Z; its complement is the unique maximal feasible Horn assignment, nonzero iff a sink SCC has no unary. A nonzero assignment opens an owner-to-fixed contact; strict lower clauses forbid new contacts and upper clauses keep diameter≤D, contradicting contact-minimality/globality. IM: owner cut stress masses A_i± have resultant magnitude A_i c_i where c_i²=δ_i²/4+(1−δ_i²/4)σ_i²; equilibrium equates to crossing diameter resultant, so A_i c_i≤D B_i and opposite projection is A_iδ_i/2>0. Thus a positive-β port has −n·v_i at most δ_i/(2c_i), giving angular windows and partner-independent count for imbalance tails.
reviews.falsification_or_counterattempt: Source report’s own notation calls r “from moving to fixed,” while its equations require r=moving−fixed. In the independent 1D control x_moving=0, y_fixed=1, v=+1, stated r=+1 gives F=max(0,−2r·v)=0 and allows s=1/2, although the new distance is 1/2; reversing the vector arrow restores the formula/floor. This scoped audit itself uses the corrected orientation and explicitly reports the source typo. Also a square control shows singleton upper safety is necessary for IM: one actual diameter lengthens while another shortens. AB amplitude x∈(0,1) shortens contact, and x∈{0,1} has no loss, so AB requires the separate unreviewed SG claim for that branch.
